question: When an AI tool can apply for jobs on our behalf, what is still ours to decide in our own career?
reflection: Open tools that anyone can inspect and adapt can spread useful skills widely, if people stay honest about what the machine wrote.

sources.subject: GitHub Copilot adds Kimi K2, Claude auto-applies for jobs, pxpipe

one_line: Open models are moving into mainstream developer tools, and everyday tasks like job applications are being handed to AI agents.

top_stories.title: Copilot offers its first open-weight model
top_stories.what: GitHub Copilot added Moonshot's Kimi K2.7, the first open-weight model in its model menu.
top_stories.why: Open models inside widely used tools make it easier to choose options that can later be hosted locally.

top_stories.title: An open tool that applies for jobs with Claude
top_stories.what: A researcher shared ai-job-search, which scores fit for a job post, drafts a tailored CV and cover letter, and uses a second agent to review the first agent's work.
top_stories.why: Employers and labour-market agencies will receive more AI-written applications, which changes how screening and fairness should be studied.

top_stories.title: Cutting AI costs by sending text as images
top_stories.what: A proxy called pxpipe turns long text context into images, which the developer says cuts Claude Code bills by up to 70%, but it can misread exact strings such as IDs.
top_stories.why: A clear example of the trade-off between cost and accuracy that every AI budget decision involves.

top_stories.title: Private redaction of patient details on a laptop
top_stories.what: OpenMed released a small model that removes personal details from clinical text and runs quickly on a Mac without the cloud.
top_stories.why: On-device redaction could let health research teams share notes for analysis without exposing patient identities.

saudi_lens.text: Local redaction of clinical text fits Saudi personal data protection rules, which favour keeping identifiable health data under tight control.

idea.title: How AI-written applications change hiring
idea.pitch: Study how recruiters judge applications drafted by AI agents and whether screening still finds the best candidates.
idea.first_step: Collect five real job adverts and generate paired human and AI-drafted applications to use in a small recruiter test.

idea_kids.title: My skills poster
idea_kids.pitch: A workshop where children draw a poster of things they are good at and practise explaining them in their own words, without any AI help.
idea_kids.first_step: Prepare a one-page template with three boxes: what I can do, how I learned it, and what I want to learn next.
